Notes/assumptions for sizing exercise (internal):
- Model baseline: redwood-4x (float16) performance profile we validated at 256-token responses: ~300 tokens/sec per A100-v4 equivalent GPU at seq=256 under p50 latency 90ms; p95 varies with batching and KV cache.
- Quantized variant redwood-4x-8bit: ~420 tokens/sec per GPU (lower memory, faster per-token) but add ~8-12ms per-token variance; need QA on quality.
- Preferred Dedicated slab topology: 1 slab = 8 x A100-v4-equivalent GPUs behind a routing / autoscale policy. We can map to fractional slabs if using burst backstop.
- Business peak requirement: 120k tokens/sec sustained. Burst up to 250k tokens/sec for up to 5 minutes.

Quick back-of-envelope:
- Using float16 GPUs @300 tps/GPU -> slab (8 GPUs) ~2400 tps.
- To hit 120k tps sustained, you need ~50 slabs (120000 / 2400 = 50). That's large; consider quantized variant or larger GPU SKUs.
- Using quantized @420 tps/GPU -> slab (8 GPUs) ~3360 tps -> ~36 slabs for 120k tps.

We should prepare two options:
A) Conservative (float16, higher margin): 60 slabs committed with 10% spare headroom; burst handled by reserved buffer + short-term autoscale to 80 slabs.
B) Cost-optimized (8-bit quantization + mixed packing): 40 slabs committed with burst backstop to 60 slabs.

I'll update the spreadsheet with a per-slab cost, estimated monthly token burn, and SLA implications. Laura — please outline operational constraints for cross-slab KV cache warming and cold-start impact during 5-minute bursts.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Pricing & Packaging

Operational notes for the proposal:
- KV cache warmup: For Falken's expected workload (many short, similar clinical prompts), prefix/KV cache hit-rate can be 65-80% after warmup — this materially increases effective tokens/sec per GPU for repeat flows. We'll model warm vs cold ratios (50/50 for conservative; 80/20 for optimistic).
- Autoscale latency: Spinning up new slabs (full GPU pool) takes ~6-10 minutes; that's too slow for 5-minute bursts. So we need a cold-buffer of idle capacity or a hot-burst pool that is pre-warmed but throttled.
- Recommended backstop: a hot-burst buffer sized to cover 60% of the burst amplitude for the first 5 minutes, with automated throttles and fallback to quantized variants. Example: if burst adds 130k tps over baseline, hot buffer = 78k tps (approx).
- Canary & downgrade plan: route to quantized models automatically at 90% committed slab utilization; if p95 > SLA, auto-fallback to lower-seq or sampling.

I'll add latency tail estimates to the spreadsheet and include a runbook paragraph for the procurement doc.

Laura Bennett
Head of Dedicated Ops

Mina — attached is the sizing workbook and the proposed slab map (proposed-dedicated-slab-map.pdf). Executive summary below:

Executive summary (two options):
1) Conservative (Recommended for earliest procurement):
   - Commit: 60 x 8-GPU slabs (480 GPUs total) running redwood-4x float16.
   - Sustained capacity: ~144k tps (300 tps/GPU * 480 GPUs).
   - p95 expectation: <= 300ms (with 10% operational headroom, warm KV cache at expected hit rates).
   - Burst approach: hot-burst buffer = 40 slabs pre-warmed (160 GPUs) to absorb first 5 minutes of peak; autoscale beyond that to 80 slabs temporary.
   - Rationale: large committed base minimizes latency tail and eliminates cold-start risk for short bursts.

2) Cost-optimized (if Falken validates quantized quality):
   - Commit: 40 x 8-GPU slabs using redwood-4x-8bit quantized profiles (320 GPUs total).
   - Sustained capacity: ~134k tps (420 tps/GPU * 320 GPUs).
   - p95 expectation: ~280-320ms depending on query mix — QA required.
   - Burst approach: hot-burst buffer = 20 slabs pre-warmed; autoscale to 60 slabs if needed.
   - Rationale: lower committed footprint, faster per-GPU token throughput, but requires QA on model parity and slightly more tail variance.

Headroom math (conservative example):
- Falken target sustained = 120k tps. With commit=60 slabs: 300 tps/GPU * 480 GPUs = 144k tps => 20% headroom.
- Burst requirement = 250k tps. With hot-burst buffer (40 slabs = 160 GPUs) additional = 160 GPUs * 300 tps/GPU = 48k tps; combined with committed gives 192k tps. To reach 250k tps we rely on autoscale to temporary 80 slabs (80*8 GPUs = 640 GPUs -> 640*300 = 192k tps additional = total 336k tps for short windows).

Operational implications & runbook highlights:
- KV cache warm window: first 15-30 minutes after deploy/major rollout — recommend staged ramp for campaign days.
- Throttle policy: Canary quantization at 90% slab utilization; circuit-breaker at 98% with graceful degradation to shorter responses.
- Procurement ask: the conservative option simplifies SLA guarantees and reduces risk of p95 breaches at the cost of higher committed spend. The cost-optimized option can be used if Falken is comfortable with an evaluation period for quantized parity and accepts slightly higher tail variance.

Attachments: falken_tps_estimates.xlsx (workbook with per-hour profiles, margin calculus, and cost estimates), proposed-dedicated-slab-map.pdf (visual slab topology and routing policy).

Please let us know which option you prefer and we can convert this into a formal SOW and offer a 30-day QA pilot for the quantized path.

Thanks,
